name: closed accordion gate
description: Cửa sắt kéo: a folding iron gate of criss-crossed flat bars that slides across a shopfront or hẻm doorway and padlocks to the wall.  You can see straight through it, and anything on the other side can see you.  Dragging it open makes a screech the whole alley hears.

name: open accordion gate
description: Cửa sắt kéo: a folding iron gate, its criss-crossed bars bunched up against the side of the doorway.

name: alley concrete
description: The poured concrete of a hẻm, cracked and patched a dozen times, stained by motorbike oil and the dirty water that runs down its middle when it rains.

name: breeze-block wall
description: Tường bông gió: a wall of cast concrete blocks pierced with flower and diamond patterns, built to let the breeze and the light through.  You can see through the holes, though nothing larger than a cat could squeeze through them.

name: patterned cement tiles
description: Gạch bông: hand-pressed cement tiles, each printed with a red-and-ochre four-petal flower, laid edge to edge so the pattern runs across the whole room.  Old Saigon houses are floored with them; they stay cool underfoot in the heat.

name: patterned cement tiles
description: Gạch bông: hand-pressed cement tiles, each printed with an eight-pointed star in blue and cream, laid edge to edge so the pattern runs across the whole room.  Old Saigon houses are floored with them; they stay cool underfoot in the heat.

name: patterned cement tiles
description: Gạch bông: hand-pressed cement tiles, each printed with a green trellis of interlocking circles, laid edge to edge so the pattern runs across the whole room.  Old Saigon houses are floored with them; they stay cool underfoot in the heat.

name: patterned cement tiles
description: Gạch bông: hand-pressed cement tiles, each printed with grey waves around a yellow medallion, laid edge to edge so the pattern runs across the whole room.  Old Saigon houses are floored with them; they stay cool underfoot in the heat.

name: glazed floor tiles
description: Shiny 40 cm glazed ceramic tiles in beige marble print, the floor every family laid when they rebuilt in the nineties.  Slippery when wet.

name: canal embankment
description: Bờ kè: the stone-faced edge of the canal, slick with green slime where the tide reaches it.  Steps lead down into the murky water.

name: corrugated metal roof
description: Mái tôn: corrugated iron sheets nailed over a shack, rusted at the seams and weighted down with old tyres against the monsoon wind.  Rain on it is deafening.

name: pink stucco wall
description: Thick colonial-era masonry rendered in a candy-pink stucco, the colour Saigon's churches are famous for.

name: terracotta tile roof
description: Mái ngói: overlapping red clay roof tiles on a timber frame, mossy in the gutters.

name: red brick wall
description: Bare red brick shipped from Toulouse a century and a half ago, never plastered: the walls of the cathedral.
